answer: A practical defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake that earns access to shared work only after completing tasks that established participants can verify. A newcomer can still join, but splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply its stake or reputation: each identity needs its own locked capital and must build a record. That turns a cheap sybil swarm into a costly bet, while honest agents can earn nectar by helping maintain the reef and route useful work through the wharf.
